signals_traced.reason: Decodes to RV32I 33/37 and M extension 8/8
Post-route LUT network contains both address-low bits and the registered load-response mux
Both miss-path offset registers exist and are driven by cpu_req_addr[1:0]
All fields are retained through the five-entry memory queue and drive load-extension LUTs
Payload maps to FDRE cells with reset tied low; valid/count own visibility
Pairs each refill word request with the value already presented to DCache, separating upstream DRAM alignment from DCache fill placement

observations: The diagnostic post-route simulation reproduces the board result by issuing an MMIO write of 0x33800000 to 0x80200020; it is not a stale-bitstream-only symptom.

Dump-directed counter tracing shows SB, SH, and LB explicitly pass, then LH, LW, LBU, and LHU explicitly take their four fail paths; later tests continue. The dispatcher did not skip, repeat, or run away.

At the CoreDCache downstream port, request 0x8010000c receives 0, request 0x80100010 receives 0x1234abcd, and request 0x80100014 receives 0x55667788. DRAM initialization places 0x1234abcd at 0x8010000c and 0x55667788 at 0x80100010, proving the response data trails the request by one word before entering DCache.

LB passes because 0x80100008 is overwritten by the preceding SW test before LB executes; the overwritten cache word no longer depends on the corrupted refill value. LH/LW/LBU/LHU still consume the shifted initial line and fail.

The cacheable range covers all 0x8010_xxxx test addresses. Refill and writeback requests reaching DramBramAdapter are word aligned; cacheable narrow-load lane selection is therefore owned by CoreDCache, not by the SoC adapter byte-write mask.

The 100 printed Synth 8-7137 warnings plus one suppression message are all reported under CoreCompressedQueue. The post-route memory-queue payload registers have R=0 and are gated by valid/count ownership, so the warnings are real cleanup items but do not establish corruption of mem_size or mem_signed.

The actual failing set is LH/LW/LBU/LHU. It is explained by the shifted initial cache line, whereas mem_size or mem_signed corruption cannot explain the correctly ordered pass/fail counter updates and the already-wrong downstream memory responses.
Post-route timing meets constraints: WNS=0.274 ns, WHS=0.088 ns, TNS=0, THS=0.
The first diagnosis was incomplete: changing resp_valid from read_valid_d2 to read_valid_d3 delays ownership but does not itself advance the registered BMG output.

The 2026-07-11 build did synthesize E:/Resources/03_competitions/26_03_jcs/2607round/superScalar/rtl/soc/DramBramAdapter.sv with read_valid_d3, and produced top.bit at 10:33. Therefore the repository fix was present in that implementation; it was not omitted by synthesis.

The generated BMG model has C_HAS_MEM_OUTPUT_REGS_A=1, C_HAS_ENA=1 and C_HAS_REGCEA=0. Its output-stage regce_i is therefore ENA. DramBramAdapter connects DRAM_0.ena only to req_valid, while CoreDCache emits a one-cycle refill request and waits. The request edge loads the addressed word into the internal memory output, but the following edge has ENA=0, so the primitive output register cannot transfer that word to douta. The next request pulse transfers the preceding word, exactly matching the observed one-word lag.

rtl/ip/DRAM_0.sv does not faithfully model that enable contract: douta <= read_data_d1 executes even when ena=0. This lets the Verilator model advance on the idle second edge and masks the FPGA failure.

root_cause.description: DramBramAdapter pulses DRAM_0.ena for only the request edge even though the selected BMG primitive output register uses the same ENA as its register clock enable. The target word reaches the internal memory output but cannot reach douta on the idle following edge; the next request pulse exposes the preceding word. Delaying resp_valid to read_valid_d3 leaves this enable/data-advance bug intact.
root_cause.evidence: The old post-route trace shows a repeatable one-word lag. The current generated DRAM_0 model independently establishes the mechanism: C_HAS_MEM_OUTPUT_REGS_A=1, C_HAS_ENA=1, C_HAS_REGCEA=0, regce_i=(C_HAS_REGCE==0)&&(C_HAS_EN==0||EN), and both the memory read and output register are edge-triggered. The latest synthesis log confirms the d3 adapter was used, while the board still reports 0x33800000.
root_cause.affected_module: rtl/soc/DramBramAdapter.sv DRAM_0.ena generation, plus rtl/ip/DRAM_0.sv enable/latency modeling

fix_recommendation.description: Keep byte-write masking unchanged. If retaining the primitive output register, make the adapter perform the complete two-edge BMG read transaction: keep the BRAM enable asserted for the output-transfer edge, keep the associated address/operation stable or explicitly register it, and assert resp_valid only when douta is usable. Preserve single-outstanding ordering and prevent the continuation enable from becoming a write. Update rtl/ip/DRAM_0.sv so douta obeys the same ENA gating; alternatively disable the primitive output register and re-derive the valid/offset latency. Verify with isolated and consecutive non-zero words in current post-implementation simulation before generating the next bitstream.
